registry_reuse.reason: Repository-local bash instrumentation of the mission loop; not a package-like AILANG capability
Test suite for a repo-local script

features.description: scripts/mission_directives.sh: emit id=<comment node id> per directive; inclusive >= since; --watermark-file read mode labelling already-processed ids and warning loudly on an unrecorded comment exactly at the watermark (the #981 signature) and on legacy bare-timestamp files; --mark <id> re-fetches, refuses unknown/non-allowlisted ids, records the id, sets line 1 to the oldest still-unprocessed allowlisted createdAt (or newest processed when none pending), prunes ids older than the watermark, writes atomically. Reading never writes the watermark. bash 3.2 / BSD tools.
acceptance_criteria: Default output unchanged except the id= token and the inclusive boundary
--mark of an unknown or non-allowlisted id exits 1 and leaves the watermark file byte-identical
Line 1 of the watermark file is always a bare ISO8601 timestamp (mission_gate0_self_notices.sh reads line 1 only)
features.notes: Implemented as planned. Also fixed a latent bash-3.2 infinite loop (`shift 2` with a missing option value). Live check: legacy watermark 2026-08-30T08:11:12Z on #852 now returns IC_kwDOP3Mz2c8AAAABReRotQ (the lost D50/D49 comment) with BOUNDARY+LEGACY warnings; mission_gate0_self_notices.sh accepted the upgraded v2 file (scratch file only, no ~/.ailang state touched). shellcheck clean.
